content:
From today, Spotify users in some countries can create managed accounts for their children even without a Premium subscription. Here are the details.

Parents and guardians with free Spotify accounts can now use the managed accounts feature.

Managed accounts are a special type of Spotify account that allows parents to provide their children with an independent, age-appropriate listening experience, equipped with parental controls. The feature was first rolled out in selected countries in 2024 for Premium Family subscribers, and has since been gradually expanded to more regions.

Through Spotify's managed accounts, parents can filter music with explicit content, block specific artists or songs, disable video playback, and keep their children's listening history separate from their own personalised recommendations — and for many parents, more importantly, it can be counted separately from Spotify Wrapped.

From today, Spotify has removed the restriction that managed accounts are only available to Premium Family subscribers. This means any parent with a Spotify account can now create a managed account for their child for free.

Spotify said the free managed account feature will first launch in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, France, Germany and the Netherlands, and is expected to expand to Europe, Latin America and other regions soon.

To set up a managed account, parents can click "Join account" in the sidebar menu on Spotify's homepage, then select "Add a child under 13". An introduction page will then appear listing the relevant features and control options, allowing parents to decide whether to allow explicit content (filtered by default) and video and Canvas content (unfiltered by default).

Managed accounts are private by default and cannot be searched, use avatars instead of uploaded photos as profile images, and do not support messaging features. Children can still enjoy personalised playlists such as Daylist and Discover Weekly, and will have a Spotify Wrapped separate from their parent's or guardian's account.

Spotify also noted that managed accounts do not require children to have their own phone. Once a managed account is added to the main account, family members can easily switch between different accounts on shared devices, while the parent or guardian's account is protected with a PIN code.

Spotify said managed accounts are for music listening only, meaning children will not be able to access other content such as podcasts and audiobooks. The company added that it will continue to listen to feedback from parents and guardians to further refine the managed account feature.

When a child reaches the legal minimum age in their country, the managed account can be converted to a regular Spotify account. Before the user turns 18, the conversion process requires parental consent; after turning 18, the user can complete the conversion themselves.
